Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

save verb

keep for later

also keep for later, set aside, put aside, save a seat, save a file, reserve, save (a file)

classical

Ov. Met. 13.829–830: pars inde bibenda servātur
Traupman 262, 374

servō, servāre, servāvī, servātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

keep, save (for later)

Traupman uses it for saving a file on a computer too.

Other words

  • reservō, reservāre, reservāvī, reservātum — keep back, save up (for later)

    verb, first conjugation; with ad and the accusative, or the dative · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.224; Caes. BC 1.36 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 370

    Lewis & Short: “to keep back, save up, qs. for future use; to reserve (very freq. and class.)”.

  • sēpōnō, sēpōnere, sēposuī, sēpositum — set aside, put by

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.132 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “to set apart, assign, appropriate, reserve, for any purpose”.

Examples

  • lac mihi semper adest niveum: pars inde bibenda servātur, partem liquefacta coāgula dūrant

    I always have snow-white milk: part of it is kept for drinking, part the rennet sets into cheese.Ov. Met. 13.829–830

  • Partem placentae patrī servā.

    Save some of the cake for Dad.composed

See also keep, save, store.

SourcesLewis & Short: servo · Lewis & Short: reservo · Lewis & Short: sepono

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 262, 370, 374.
